title: The global housing crisis is converting affordability, displacement, informality, climate exposure, and urban delivery into one access problem
source_unit: UN-Habitat, World Cities Report 2026: The Global Housing Crisis: Pathways to Action, SDG 11 Global Report 2026, and Urban Content in NDC 3.0
geography: Global cities, urban households, informal settlements, displaced populations, national climate plans, and countries reporting to UN-Habitat

denominator.unit: global population and urban housing conditions covered by UN-Habitat estimates

people_without_secure_adequate_housing.unit: billion people lacking access to secure, safe, and adequate housing

informal_settlement_population.unit: billion or more people living in informal settlements and slums

housing_deficit_2023.unit: million housing units in the global deficit in 2023

housing_deficit_2010.unit: million housing units in the global deficit in 2010

observations.method: UN-Habitat global synthesis of housing deficits, inadequate housing, informal settlements, and the social, economic, and environmental functions of adequate housing.
observations.uncertainty: Global estimates combine different national definitions and data quality; a housing deficit does not directly measure affordability, tenure security, service access, or individual housing trajectories in every location.
observations.subgroup: Urban households, informal-settlement residents, renters, owners, displaced people, low-income communities, and cities with different land and service systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Housing construction, upgrading, public land, rental protections, and community-led solutions can reduce deficits without requiring identical tenure models across cities.

denominator.unit: global evictions and housing-related displacement cases estimated by UN-Habitat research

people_evicted.unit: million people estimated to have been evicted globally between 2003 and 2023

housing_crisis_drivers.value: insufficient investment, rapid urbanization, economic instability, conflict, disasters, and climate-related displacement

housing_consequence_path.value: housing affects livelihoods, security, social well-being, employment, public-service access, health, and economic opportunity

observations.method: UN-Habitat report synthesis of eviction research and the interacting economic, conflict, disaster, and climate drivers of housing insecurity.
observations.uncertainty: The eviction estimate is a global research estimate rather than a complete administrative count; it does not establish the relative contribution of each driver or the later outcomes for every affected household.
observations.subgroup: Evicted households, displaced populations, tenants, informal-settlement residents, disaster-affected communities, and local governments.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some households move voluntarily or secure improved housing after displacement; prevention, compensation, legal assistance, and upgrading can change the trajectory even when initial housing loss is severe.

observations.period: 2026; urban housing as a multi-dimensional city-system outcome

denominator.unit: UN-Habitat World Cities Report framework for the global housing crisis

interlocking_dimensions.value: affordability, displacement, informality, resilience and sustainability, and liveability
interlocking_dimensions.unit: five dimensions of the global housing crisis

sdg11_linkages.value: housing conditions shape transport, urban planning, environmental quality, disaster-risk reduction, public space, heritage, and local implementation

data_gap.value: urban data remain insufficiently disaggregated to understand inequalities affecting vulnerable people at city and neighbourhood levels

observations.method: UN-Habitat SDG 11 and World Cities Report frameworks linking housing conditions and policy choices to urban outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: A framework identifies connected mechanisms but does not estimate causal effects between each housing dimension and each urban outcome; city and neighbourhood data remain uneven.
observations.subgroup: Cities, neighbourhoods, vulnerable residents, public-service users, planners, housing providers, and local implementation institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Integrated planning can create co-benefits, but transport, public space, resilience, and housing interventions may also compete for land, funding, and political attention.

observations.period: 2026; Nationally Determined Contributions 3.0 submitted through mid-April 2026

denominator.unit: third-generation Nationally Determined Contributions analyzed by UN-Habitat

well_developed_urban_content.unit: percent of submitted NDCs 3.0 featuring well-developed urban content, compared with 49 percent in the previous cycle

housing_informal_settlements_priority.value: almost half of submitted NDCs include housing and informal settlements as a cross-cutting climate priority

urban_delivery_mechanisms.unit: approximately percent of NDCs including concrete urban delivery mechanisms

governance_route.value: multilevel governance and capacity-building increasingly connect national climate commitments to cities and regions

observations.method: UN-Habitat comparative review of 142 third-generation national climate plans submitted by mid-April 2026.
observations.uncertainty: Plan content is an intention and implementation signal, not evidence of funded delivery, emissions reduction, housing improvement, or equal local capacity; the 75 percent figure is reported approximately.
observations.subgroup: National governments, city and regional authorities, housing agencies, informal settlements, climate-vulnerable residents, and multilevel delivery partners.
observations.counterinterpretation: More urban content may reflect stronger planning language without additional resources; conversely, local delivery mechanisms can produce progress even when national plan language is thin.

related_sources.claim: UN-Habitat SDG 11 report places housing at the centre of urban progress across transport, planning, environment, resilience, public space, heritage, and implementation.
UN-Habitat review of urban content in third-generation national climate plans.
UN SDG 11 indicators provide complementary global measures of urban land, public space, transport, and resilience.

boundary: This record adds a place and housing route linking affordability, displacement, informality, liveability, climate exposure, urban services, and multilevel delivery. It is not a city-specific rent estimate, a causal evaluation of housing policy, a household panel, or respondent-level microdata analysis.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UN-Habitat World Cities Report 2026, SDG 11 Global Report 2026, Urban Content in NDC 3.0, and complementary UN SDG 11 materials were reviewed; housing, displacement, urban-system, climate-plan, and measurement-boundary claims were cross-checked.
